channel.title: Killed by AI — The AI Graveyard
channel.description: A digital cemetery for discontinued AI models, apps, startups, and hardware.

item.title: Amazon Lookout for Equipment — Killed by AWS (2026-10-07)
item.description: AWS's managed ML service that learned the normal behavior of industrial equipment from sensor data and flagged anomalies before failures. It went GA on April 8, 2021, closed to new customers in late 2024 and was discontinued on October 7, 2026, after which the console and all resources became inaccessible. AWS pointed customers to the native anomaly detection added to AWS IoT SiteWise in July 2025, plus a GitHub repo of migration scripts. Its siblings Lookout for Metrics and Lookout for Vision were already gone, both in October 2025.

item.title: Gemini API Antigravity Agent (05-2026 preview) — Killed by Google (2026-10-05)
item.description: antigravity-preview-05-2026 was the first version of Google's managed Antigravity agent in the Gemini API, launched May 19, 2026 alongside Managed Agents. On September 17 Google shipped antigravity-preview-09-2026, which swapped the old file tools for new ones (write_file became write_to_file and replace_file_content, read_file became view_file, list_files became list_dir), moved tool parameters to PascalCase, replaced full-file rewrites with line-range edits, and set the old agent's shutdown for October 5. It lived 139 days. Apps that only read its output changed one string; anyone running its tools locally or parsing its function calls had to rewrite code. The Antigravity IDE is unaffected.

item.title: Kimi K2.7 Code (GitHub Copilot & Microsoft Foundry) — Killed by GitHub / Microsoft (2026-10-02)
item.description: Moonshot's open-weight coding model went generally available in GitHub Copilot on July 1, 2026 and was removed from every Copilot surface on October 2, 93 days later, with Kimi K3 named as its replacement. The next day Microsoft Foundry's preview deployment (version 2026-06-12) hit its October 3 retirement date with no replacement listed. The same Copilot changelog also cleared out Gemini 3.5 Flash, Gemini 3.6 Flash and Claude Opus 4.7. Moonshot's own API still lists kimi-k2.7-code as active; only Microsoft let go.

item.title: Mistral OCR 4.0 — Killed by Mistral (2026-09-30)
item.description: Mistral released OCR 4 (mistral-ocr-4-0) on June 23, 2026, supporting 170 languages and claiming independent annotators preferred it over every leading OCR and document-AI system tested, with a 72% average win rate. OCR 4.1 took over the mistral-ocr-4 and mistral-ocr-latest aliases on July 16 and went GA on August 31. The changelog marked 4.0 deprecated on September 29 and retired it on September 30, at the same price as its replacement: one day's formal notice. It lived 99 days and died the same day as Leanstral 1.5.

item.title: Appsmith AI — Killed by Appsmith (2026-09-30)
item.description: The low-code platform's managed AI datasource, merged in January 2024, which ran on model credentials Appsmith paid for. A pull request opened July 17, 2026 spelled out the problem: 'Appsmith pays for LLM tokens behind the managed Appsmith AI plugin.' From release 2.3 on August 13, new Appsmith AI datasources and queries were blocked with errors AE-DTS-4031 and AE-DTS-4032, and on September 30, 2026 every existing one stopped working, whether or not the instance had been upgraded. Free AI, it turns out, has a meter.

item.title: Microsoft Copilot Labs — Killed by Microsoft (2026-09-29)
item.description: Microsoft's experimental sandbox for consumer Copilot, launched October 1, 2024 with Think Deeper, with Copilot Vision following soon after. Its biggest graduates had long since moved into the main app. On September 29, 2026 Labs was retired as part of the unified Copilot app, and Microsoft pointed early-access users to 'Frontier in Copilot' and the MAI Playground. What remained, experiments such as 3D and audio generation, died with it.

item.title: Google Mixboard — Killed by Google (2026-09-28)
item.description: Google Labs' AI concepting board: an open canvas where Google's Nano Banana image model generated, remixed and edited pictures into mood boards and presentations. It launched as a US-only public beta on September 23, 2025, spread to more than 180 countries that October, and was taken offline on September 28, 2026, a year and five days later. Google said it had 'learned a lot from this experiment' and would apply the lessons to 'future Google Labs explorations and creative tooling.' It follows Whisk and Doppl, two other Labs experiments Google shut down on April 30, 2026.

item.title: Perplexity Sonar Chat Completions API — Killed by Perplexity (2026-09-27)
item.description: Perplexity's search-grounded chat-completions API, launched January 21, 2025 with Sonar and Sonar Pro and later joined by sonar-reasoning-pro and sonar-deep-research. Support ended September 27, 2026, when the Agent API became the main surface. Synchronous and streaming calls are being quietly rewritten as Agent API presets (sonar and sonar-pro become 'fast', reasoning-pro 'low', deep-research 'high'); asynchronous requests are simply no longer supported. Some developers on migrated accounts reported HTTP 403 'agent_api_migration_required' errors from the old endpoint. The Sonar model lives on inside the Agent API; the API that carried its name does not.

item.title: Excel =COPILOT() Function — Killed by Microsoft (2026-09-14)
item.description: A worksheet function that put an LLM inside a cell: =COPILOT(prompt, range) could summarize, classify or tag rows in place. It reached Beta Channel Insiders with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license on August 18, 2025, and Excel for the web through Frontier later, with Microsoft's own warning, as Windows Central reported, not to use it for numerical calculations or anything with legal, regulatory or compliance implications. In a spreadsheet, that rules out a lot. It never left preview: message-center notice MC1454373 retired it on September 14, 2026, and the roadmap entry said simply, 'We have decided not to move forward with this feature.'

item.title: TruckSmarter Dispatch — Killed by Undisclosed Acquirer (2026-09-04)
item.description: TruckSmarter ran a free load board used by more than 500,000 carriers. In September 2025, alongside a $16M round led by Socium Ventures, it launched Dispatch, an AI chat interface where drivers asked for freight in plain language and software agents handled the bidding and booking. On Tuesday, September 1, 2026 it told users it was being acquired, and on Friday, September 4 it switched the app off. Nobody will say who bought it; OTR Solutions, which had bought the factoring and banking arm in November 2025, says it wasn't them.

item.title: Rilo — Killed by Adobe (2026-09-02)
item.description: An Indian startup founded in 2025 by IIT Bombay alumni Dhruv Jaglan and Georgi Boby, selling AI agents for marketing work described in plain English: competitor intelligence, campaign research, social outreach, content repurposing and sales-call analysis. It raised $1M from Peak XV Partners, DeVC and Day Zero Ventures at a $10M valuation and, by Jaglan's account, reached 10,000 users within months of launch. On September 2, 2026 Adobe acquired it in an undisclosed deal that licensed its technology and brought its six-person team into Adobe. The platform shut down after the deal; no switch-off date was published.

item.title: Raptor mini (GitHub Copilot) — Killed by GitHub / Microsoft (2026-09-01)
item.description: GitHub's own model, a fine-tuned GPT-5 mini pitched for fast, accurate inline suggestions and explanations. It entered public preview on November 10, 2025, only ever in VS Code's Copilot Chat, and was listed as generally available by August 2026. On September 1 GitHub removed it from Copilot Chat, inline edits, ask and agent modes and code completions, in the same changelog that retired a batch of Claude and Gemini models. Unlike those, Raptor mini existed nowhere else: 295 days, start to finish. Its replacement is MAI-Code-1.1-Flash, whose predecessor was pulled from Copilot nine days later.

item.title: Microsoft Edge Real-Time Video Translation — Killed by Microsoft (2026-08-27)
item.description: On-device AI dubbing for the web. You hovered over a video, clicked Translate, and Edge downloaded a roughly 200 MB language model and replaced the audio track in real time. Shown off at Build 2024, it shipped in Edge 141 in October 2025, but only on Windows PCs with at least 12 GB of RAM and a four-core CPU, and only in select markets. Edge 152 began retiring it on August 27, 2026, less than eleven months later, in the same release that killed Edge Drop. Microsoft gave no reason.

item.title: Microsoft Copilot Groups, Podcasts & Deep Research — Killed by Microsoft (2026-08-18)
item.description: Three headline features of Microsoft's consumer Copilot were retired from August 18, 2026, as Microsoft merged its consumer Copilot and Microsoft 365 Copilot apps into one. AI-generated Podcasts and Deep Research had debuted at Copilot's April 2025 anniversary event; Groups, which let up to 32 people share one Copilot chat, arrived in the October 2025 Fall Release alongside Mico, the animated blob, which began leaving Copilot Voice in waves that same August. Copilot chief Jacob Andreou had reportedly told staff the app had to earn 'the right to exist' in people's lives.

item.title: Google Earth AI Image Generation — Killed by Google (2026-07-31)
item.description: On July 30, 2026 Google put Nano Banana 2 inside Google Earth on the web: zoom to any spot on the planet, click 'create image', and describe what should be there instead. A BBC journalist and other critics pointed out that one of the most trusted sources of visual evidence for journalists and researchers now had a fake-imagery button. By the next day Google said it had seen people 'sharing screenshots of generated imagery that appear to violate our policies' and rolled the feature back while it worked on stronger guardrails. It lived about a day.

item.title: Meta AI Instagram @-Mention Images — Killed by Meta (2026-07-10)
item.description: Launched alongside Meta Superintelligence Labs' Muse Image generator on July 7, 2026, it let you @-mention a public Instagram account in Meta AI and generate images of that person, pitched for birthday cards and group-trip memes. It was on by default: account owners were never notified, and the only protection was an opt-out in Instagram's settings. Users and talent agencies including CAA pushed back, and critics pointed to the obvious non-consensual imagery risk. Three days later Meta posted a brief update to its announcement: 'this feature missed the mark, so it's no longer available.'

item.title: Gemini CLI (Free & Consumer Tiers) — Killed by Google (2026-06-18)
item.description: Google's open-source (Apache-2.0) terminal coding agent launched June 25, 2025 and passed 100,000 GitHub stars and 6,000 merged pull requests. At I/O on May 19, 2026 Google folded its developer tools under the Antigravity brand, and on June 18 Gemini CLI and the Gemini Code Assist IDE extensions stopped serving free users, Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers and free individual Code Assist users. Their replacement, Antigravity CLI (agy), ships as a binary with no public repo. Code Assist Standard and Enterprise licenses and paid API keys kept access, and Google still updates the open-source repo for them: the code survived, the free users didn't.

item.title: LOVO AI — Killed by itself (2026-05-27)
item.description: A Berkeley AI voiceover and voice-cloning startup, founded in 2019, behind the Genny text-to-speech studio. LOVO filed for Chapter 7 liquidation on May 27, 2026, listing $245,224 in assets against $17,788 in liabilities. The filing landed less than three weeks before a June 16 hearing on its motion to dismiss Lehrman & Sage v. Lovo, a class action by voice actors who say their voices were cloned without permission; the bankruptcy automatically stayed the case. Paying customers had been reporting on Trustpilot since late April that they were locked out of their accounts.

item.title: Soul Machines — Killed by itself (2026-02-05)
item.description: A New Zealand maker of AI 'Digital People' avatars, co-founded in 2016 by Greg Cross and Mark Sagar, a two-time Sci-Tech Academy Award winner for facial-capture work at Weta Digital. It raised more than US$135M (about NZ$225M) from backers including Horizons Ventures, SoftBank Vision Fund 2, Salesforce Ventures and Temasek. On February 5, 2026 KPMG's Leon Bowker and Luke Norman were appointed receivers. On September 28, 2026 AppDirect announced it had acquired Soul Machines on undisclosed terms and would build the avatars into Devs.ai, so the faces live on with a different employer.

item.title: PlayAI (PlayHT) — Killed by Meta (2025-12-31)
item.description: PlayHT began in 2016 as a browser extension that read articles aloud and grew into a text-to-speech, voice-cloning and voice-agent platform, later renamed PlayAI. Founders Hammad Syed and Mahmoud Felfel went through Y Combinator and raised a $21M seed round in November 2024 led by Kindred Ventures and 500 Global. In July 2025 Meta acquired the company and took the entire team to work on voice for Meta AI, AI Characters and wearables. The API was given until December 31, 2025, and voice-agent frameworks such as Pipecat deprecated their PlayHT integrations ahead of the cutoff.

item.title: Dot (New Computer) — Killed by Its Own Founders (2025-10-05)
item.description: A personalized AI companion app from New Computer, co-founded by Sam Whitmore and former Apple designer Jason Yuan, that launched on iOS in June 2024. On September 5, 2025 the founders announced that their 'shared Northstar had diverged' and that, rather than compromise either vision, they would 'wind down operations'. The app stopped on October 5, 2025, after a month for data export. The company claimed 'hundreds of thousands' of users; Appfigures counted about 24,500 lifetime iOS downloads, and there was never an Android app.

item.title: Esperanto Technologies — Killed by Deep-Pocketed Rivals (2025-07-01)
item.description: A RISC-V AI-inference chipmaker founded in 2014 by Transmeta co-founder Dave Ditzel. Its 7nm ET-SoC-1 packed 1,088 small ET-Minion cores and four larger ET-Maxion cores onto one chip. A $58M Series B in November 2018 brought equity funding to $63M, plus a $1.5M PPP loan in 2020. In July 2025 it closed most operations, keeping only the staff needed to sell its IP, after rivals offered prospective employees up to four times its pay. Ainekko (Nekko.ai) bought the IP that October and is open-sourcing it.

item.title: Untether AI — Killed by AMD (2025-06-05)
item.description: A Toronto AI-inference chip startup selling speedAI accelerators and the imAIgine SDK. PitchBook data cited by The Logic puts its funding at US$168M from backers including CPP Investments, Intel Capital and Radical Ventures, with the last major round in July 2021. In early June 2025 AMD took its engineering team in an undisclosed deal, and Untether said it would 'no longer be supplying or supporting our speedAI products and imAIgine software development kit.' The engineers went to work on AMD's AI compiler, kernel and chip-design efforts.

item.title: Notion Mail — Killed by Notion (2026-09-22)
item.description: Notion's AI email client lasted 17 months. Notion shut the web, desktop and iOS apps on September 22, explaining that more than half its users were already handling email through agents without ever opening the inbox. The Gmail connector and email-writing agents live on; the inbox does not.

item.title: OpenAI GPT-5.4-Cyber — Killed by OpenAI (2026-10-01)
item.description: The 'cyber-permissive' GPT-5.4 variant built for vetted security defenders — the model that could reverse-engineer binaries and anchored OpenAI's Trusted Access for Cyber program — was shut down October 1 after five and a half months, with three weeks' notice. OpenAI's replacement advice: 'the most capable cyber model available to you.'

item.title: Mistral Leanstral 1.5 — Killed by Mistral (2026-09-30)
item.description: Mistral's Lean 4 formal-proof model was retired on September 30, exactly as its own launch note promised: 'We released Leanstral 1.5... This model will be retired on September 30, 2026.' A 92-day advertised lifespan, announced in the same sentence as its birth, with no replacement named.

item.title: Amazon Mechanical Turk — Killed by Amazon (2026-09-30)
item.description: The marketplace Jeff Bezos called "artificial artificial intelligence" closed on September 30 after 21 years — the human crowd, 500,000 strong at its peak, that labelled a generation of AI training data. Amazon shut SageMaker Ground Truth and Amazon Augmented AI the same day, leaving human-data work entirely. The official reason was an internal review of its programs; the obvious one is that the models MTurk workers trained now do MTurk's work.

item.title: Amazon Nova Canvas & Nova Reel — Killed by Amazon (2026-09-30)
item.description: The image and video half of Amazon's first Nova generation, launched at re:Invent 2024, left Bedrock on September 30 — two weeks after Nova Premier and Sonic. AWS pointed image users to Nova 2 Lite and video users to a rival's model, Luma Ray v2.

item.title: OpenAI davinci-002, babbage-002 & gpt-3.5-turbo-instruct — Killed by OpenAI (2026-09-28)
item.description: The end of the GPT-3 base-model lineage, retired September 28. davinci-002 and babbage-002 shipped in August 2023 and inherited the job when the original ada/babbage/curie/davinci died in January 2024; gpt-3.5-turbo-instruct, the instruct-tuned completions model, joined them that September. The same cutoff also took a fourth model: gpt-3.5-turbo-1106, the chat snapshot from OpenAI's November 2023 DevDay. OpenAI's suggested replacement is gpt-5.6-terra; their fine-tuned versions outlive them by 25 days.

item.title: Reve AI Image Generation — Killed by OpenAI (2026-09-27)
item.description: Reve's image generator — briefly the top-ranked text-to-image model on launch in March 2025 — shut off at noon Pacific on September 27, the price of an investment from OpenAI, which also took its AI research team to lead multimodal work. The API went dark on August 14 and sign-ups stopped September 17; users have until October 31 to export, and September fees are refunded. The company survives; the product does not.
